{% endif %} {%- comment -%} Where the student actually works. This is the first thing they need and it used to be a grey italic line at the very bottom of the page, under the whole brief - so the answer to "where do I write this?" sat below the thing it was needed for. `repo_url` is the cohort org's repo list filtered to this assignment rather than one student's address: the page is public and identical for everyone, and GitHub shows a signed-in student only the repos they can see, so the filter lands on their own. Absent while the assignment is pending - there is nothing at the other end of it yet. {%- endcomment -%} {%- comment -%} `submit_shape` (site.py, off `course.submit_shape` and so off the assignment's own grading_config.yml) is the SHAPE in one word - `external`, `github-private`, `github-public`, `github-student-choice`. `external` is handed in off GitHub - Moodle, Kaggle, in class - and NO repo is created for it at all. So there is nothing to open and nothing to name: the brief below says where the work goes, and `submit_url` puts a button on it when the assignment names an address. This block used to print off `repo_url` alone, so a Moodle assignment told the whole cohort that a push to `main` was its submission. `escape`: `repo_name` is a SHAPE, `-`, and those angle brackets make `` an unknown HTML tag that the browser silently drops - so the name rendered as `assignment-1-` with the useful half missing. `data-dsl-repo`: the repo SHAPE, and the one thing on the page that a reader with a profile can be told exactly. open_in.html rewrites every one of these to the real name (`assignment-1-jane`) and repoints every `data-dsl-repo-url` beside them at that repo, so a student stops reading `` and substituting themselves. Marked rather than matched on the prose, because the sentences around them are reworded. {%- endcomment -%} {%- comment -%} `handout_pending` gates the whole block: an assignment still to come has no brief to read and no address to go to, so a callout would answer a question the page has not asked yet. It is also why the external arm says only WHERE the work is handed in and never "no repository is created": a cohort handed out before that arm existed has the repos it was given, and this would be telling those students their own repo is not there. ONE arm for every shape that has a repo: one button, one link, and the `case` below branches only the SENTENCE. A shape that copied the button carried its own copy of the open_in.html contract to keep in step, and the two drifted the first time one of them was reworded. A `github-public` assignment is portfolio work - a hackathon, a showcase - and the whole internet can read the repo from the moment it is handed out, so the callout a student reads BEFORE their first push is where that has to be said; saying it in the brief alone leaves it to whoever wrote the brief. EVERY arm but the default one names the gradebook, and for one reason: the default is the only shape with a Feedback issue (`course.has_feedback_issue` - a thread in a public repo, or in a repo the whole cohort reads, is a published mark), so it is the only page whose reader can expect their marks where the work is. On the other four, the private `grades-` repo is the only place feedback ever appears, and a student who does not know that is a student who thinks nobody marked their work. `github-student-choice` is the same repo with the flag handed over: it starts private, the student is its admin, and the toolkit puts it back to private until the grading cutoff has passed (`scheduler._reprivatise_student_repos`). Both halves of that belong HERE - a student who reads only "you are an admin" publishes their work on day one and finds it closed again an hour later - and it has no Feedback issue either, for the reason the public arm does not. `repo_name_is_shape` (site.py) is what decides whether the two data attributes are written at all. `shared` is the one shape whose `repo_name` is a REAL repo and not a shape: there is a single private drop box for the whole cohort, and what is the student's own is a folder in it (`submit_path`). There is nothing in that name for open_in.html to substitute a handle into, and rewriting it would point every reader at a repo that does not exist - so the flag is false and the markers are left off. {%- endcomment -%} {% unless page.handout_pending %} {% if page.submit_shape == "external" %}
